title: Index Architecture and Design Guide - SQL Server
subcategory: Rowstore, columnstore and memory-optimized index design
engineering_principles: RECOMMENDED: few narrow rowstore indexes for high-throughput OLTP, clustered columnstore for analytics; clustered keys narrow, unique, ever-increasing, immutable; do not index speculatively, monitor and remove unused indexes.
practical_examples: Single int or bigint IDENTITY clustered key satisfies all properties; uniqueidentifier is wider and not ever-increasing unless sequential; move non-predicate columns to INCLUDE.
why_it_matters: Gives the most explicit vendor split between OLTP and OLAP initial index design.
notes: Date is ms.date; page updated_at 2026-10-19.

title: Columnstore indexes: Overview - SQL Server
engineering_principles: RECOMMENDED: clustered columnstore for fact tables and large dimensions; rowstore for seek-heavy transactional work. CONTEXTUAL: nonclustered columnstore for real-time analytics on OLTP tables.
practical_examples: Rowgroups hold up to 1,048,576 rows; small loads go to a B-tree deltastore; batch mode typically gives 2-4x.
why_it_matters: Defines when a schema should use column storage rather than B-trees.
notes: The up-to-10x figures are vendor claims.

title: Partitioned Tables and Indexes - SQL Server
engineering_principles: MANDATORY: unique indexes and clustered keys must contain the partitioning column when aligned. RECOMMENDED: avoid many hundreds or thousands of partitions unless strictly necessary. Partitioning rarely improves performance in OLTP systems.
practical_examples: Monthly RANGE RIGHT function on datetime; switch partitions out to an archive table for retention.
why_it_matters: Directly counters partitioning as a default OLTP performance tactic.
notes: Limit of 15,000 partitions.

title: Create Indexed Views - SQL Server
engineering_principles: MANDATORY if used: SCHEMABINDING, deterministic definition, required SET options, COUNT_BIG with GROUP BY. CONTEXTUAL: DML can degrade significantly on referenced tables, so test first.
practical_examples: Sales.vOrders aggregate with a unique clustered index on OrderDate, ProductID, matched without being named in the query.
why_it_matters: Shows the write cost of precomputed aggregates on transactional tables.
notes: Automatic matching is edition-dependent; Standard edition needs NOEXPAND.

title: PostgreSQL Documentation: Index Types
engineering_principles: RECOMMENDED: B-tree default. CONTEXTUAL: GIN for multi-valued data, GiST for geometric and nearest-neighbor, BRIN for columns correlated with physical order, hash for equality only.
practical_examples: LIKE 'foo%' can use a B-tree, LIKE '%bar' cannot.
why_it_matters: Maps data shape and operators to an index type.
notes: PostgreSQL 18.6 docs. Page does not state BRIN size.

title: PostgreSQL Documentation: Multicolumn Indexes
engineering_principles: RECOMMENDED: use multicolumn indexes sparingly; more than three columns is unlikely to help unless usage is extremely stylized.
practical_examples: CREATE INDEX test2_mm_idx ON test2 (major, minor).
why_it_matters: States the exact rule for which predicates bound a B-tree scan.
notes: PostgreSQL 18.6 docs. Gives no general column-order preference.

title: PostgreSQL Documentation: Index-Only Scans and Covering Indexes
engineering_principles: CONTEXTUAL: index-only scans win only if a significant fraction of heap pages are all-visible; be conservative with payload columns, especially wide ones.
practical_examples: CREATE INDEX tab_x_y ON tab(x) INCLUDE (y).
why_it_matters: Covering indexes pay off less on frequently changing PostgreSQL tables.
notes: PostgreSQL 18.6 docs.

title: PostgreSQL Documentation: Partial Indexes
engineering_principles: CONTEXTUAL: exclude common or uninteresting values, or enforce conditional uniqueness. Avoid sets of non-overlapping partial indexes as a partitioning substitute.
practical_examples: CREATE UNIQUE INDEX tests_success_constraint ON tests (subject, target) WHERE success.
why_it_matters: Enables smaller indexes and conditional business rules.
notes: PostgreSQL 18.6 docs. Parameterized clauses do not work with a partial index.

title: PostgreSQL Documentation: Indexes Introduction
engineering_principles: RECOMMENDED: remove indexes that are seldom or never used; run ANALYZE so the planner has current statistics.
practical_examples: CREATE INDEX test1_id_index ON test1 (id).
why_it_matters: Establishes that every index has an ongoing write cost.
notes: PostgreSQL 18.6 docs.

title: PostgreSQL Documentation: CREATE INDEX
engineering_principles: CONTEXTUAL: fillfactor 50-90 can smooth page splits on write-heavy tables; 100 only for tables certain to be static. RECOMMENDED: CONCURRENTLY for production builds.
practical_examples: CREATE UNIQUE INDEX title_idx ON films (title) WITH (fillfactor = 70).
why_it_matters: Covers physical index settings and safe rollout on live tables.
notes: PostgreSQL 18.6 docs. Default B-tree fillfactor is 90.

title: PostgreSQL Documentation: Constraints
engineering_principles: RECOMMENDED: it is often a good idea to index referencing columns; PostgreSQL does not do so automatically because it is not always needed.
practical_examples: CREATE INDEX ON order_items (order_id).
why_it_matters: Basis for an engine-specific FK indexing rule.
notes: PostgreSQL 18.6 docs.

title: PostgreSQL Documentation: Table Partitioning
engineering_principles: MANDATORY: unique and primary key constraints must include all partition key columns. CONTEXTUAL: worthwhile only for very large tables; rule of thumb is table size exceeding server memory. RECOMMENDED: partition on the columns most common in WHERE clauses.
practical_examples: measurement table PARTITION BY RANGE (logdate) with monthly partitions.
why_it_matters: Partitioning choices constrain keys and uniqueness in the logical schema.
notes: PostgreSQL 18.6 docs. FK behaviour on partitioned tables was not captured.

title: PostgreSQL Documentation: Using EXPLAIN
engineering_principles: RECOMMENDED: compare estimated and actual rows; wrap data-modifying EXPLAIN ANALYZE in a transaction and roll back, because the statement really executes.
practical_examples: Seq Scan, Bitmap Heap Scan and Index Scan chosen on tenk1 as selectivity changes.
why_it_matters: The verification method for any index recommendation.
notes: PostgreSQL 18.6 docs.

title: PostgreSQL Documentation: PREPARE
engineering_principles: CONTEXTUAL: first five executions use custom plans, then a generic plan unless its cost is much higher; override with plan_cache_mode when the estimate is badly off.
practical_examples: EXPLAIN EXECUTE shows $n parameters when a generic plan is in use.
why_it_matters: Explains plan regressions for parameterized OLTP queries.
notes: PostgreSQL 18.6 docs. Page has no explicit skew warning.

title: PostgreSQL Documentation: UUID Functions
engineering_principles: CONTEXTUAL: uuidv7 generates time-ordered values; uuidv4 and gen_random_uuid generate random values.
practical_examples: uuidv7() with an optional interval shift.
why_it_matters: Supplies the time-ordered option in the UUID primary key debate.
notes: PostgreSQL 18.6 docs. Page makes no index-locality claim.

title: PostgreSQL 18 Release Notes
engineering_principles: CONTEXTUAL: skip scan lets multicolumn B-trees serve queries without restrictions on early columns, softening strict leading-column rules on version 18 and later.
practical_examples: Skip scan where useful restrictions exist only on later indexed columns.
why_it_matters: Marks where older index advice has become version-dependent.

title: MySQL 8.4 Reference Manual: Optimization and Indexes
engineering_principles: RECOMMENDED: do not index every column; unnecessary indexes waste space and optimizer time and add DML cost.
practical_examples: Chapter covers column, multiple-column, invisible, descending and generated-column indexes.
why_it_matters: Vendor statement against blanket indexing.

title: MySQL 8.4 Reference Manual: Multiple-Column Indexes
engineering_principles: MANDATORY engine behaviour: lookups require a leftmost prefix of the index.
practical_examples: INDEX name (last_name, first_name) is not used for first_name alone.
why_it_matters: Defines which query shapes one composite index can serve.
notes: No selectivity-ordering guidance on the page.

title: MySQL 8.4 Reference Manual: Comparison of B-Tree and Hash Indexes
engineering_principles: CONTEXTUAL: hash indexes serve only = and <=>, cannot speed ORDER BY, and need whole keys.
practical_examples: LIKE 'Patrick%' uses a B-tree; LIKE '%Patrick%' does not.
why_it_matters: Shows why B-tree remains the general default.
notes: Page names only the MEMORY engine for selectable hash indexes.

title: MySQL 8.4 Reference Manual: Invisible Indexes
engineering_principles: RECOMMENDED: test index removal by making it invisible before dropping it.
practical_examples: ALTER TABLE t1 ALTER INDEX i_idx INVISIBLE.
why_it_matters: Gives a reversible step for index pruning.
notes: Primary keys cannot be invisible.

title: MySQL 8.4 Reference Manual: FOREIGN KEY Constraints
engineering_principles: MANDATORY engine behaviour: an index with FK columns first must exist and is created automatically if absent.
practical_examples: The implicit index may be silently dropped when another index can enforce the constraint.
why_it_matters: The counterpoint to PostgreSQL in the FK indexing rule.

title: MySQL 8.4 Reference Manual: Clustered and Secondary Indexes
engineering_principles: RECOMMENDED: define a primary key on every table and keep it short, because each secondary index record stores it.
practical_examples: Add an auto-increment column when no natural unique non-null key exists.
why_it_matters: PK width multiplies across all secondary indexes.

title: MySQL 8.4 Reference Manual: Type Conversion in Expression Evaluation
engineering_principles: RECOMMENDED: match predicate types to column types; a string column compared with a number cannot use its index for lookup.
practical_examples: SELECT * FROM tbl_name WHERE str_col=1 cannot use the index on str_col.
why_it_matters: Column data types determine index usability.

title: Oracle Database Concepts: Indexes and Index-Organized Tables
engineering_principles: RECOMMENDED: bitmap indexes for low-cardinality, rarely modified warehouse data, and not for many OLTP applications; consider indexing FK columns to avoid full table locks on parent changes.
practical_examples: CREATE INDEX emp_fname_uppercase_idx ON employees (UPPER(first_name)).
why_it_matters: Clearest workload rationale for bitmap versus B-tree.
notes: Requested /23/ URL; content served was labelled Oracle AI Database 26 with a /26/ path.

title: Oracle VLDB and Partitioning Guide: Partitioning Concepts
subcategory: Strategies, pruning, local and global indexes
engineering_principles: RECOMMENDED: generally global indexes for OLTP and local indexes for DSS; consider partitioning tables over 2 GB and historical tables.
practical_examples: Weekly partitions over two years, with pruning to one of 104 partitions; partition exchange load.
why_it_matters: The most workload-explicit guidance on partitioned index type.
notes: Requested /23/ URL; content served was labelled Oracle AI Database 26ai. The 2 GB threshold differs from PostgreSQL's rule of thumb.

title: Oracle Data Warehousing Guide: Basic Query Rewrite for Materialized Views
engineering_principles: RECOMMENDED for warehouses: precomputed joins and aggregates with transparent rewrite. CONTEXTUAL: STALE_TOLERATED risks inaccurate results.
practical_examples: join_sales_time_product_mv created with ENABLE QUERY REWRITE.
why_it_matters: Materialized views can be added or dropped without changing application SQL.
notes: Content names Oracle AI Database; no version number or date shown.

title: MongoDB Database Manual: Indexes
engineering_principles: CONTEXTUAL: indexes are expensive on collections with a high write-to-read ratio.
practical_examples: Automatic, non-droppable unique index on _id.
why_it_matters: Extends the read-write index trade-off to document stores.
notes: 9.0 docs. Index limits, covered queries and TTL sub-pages not fetched.

title: The ESR (Equality, Sort, Range) Guideline
engineering_principles: RECOMMENDED: equality fields first; sort before range to avoid in-memory sorts, or range before sort when the range is very selective.
practical_examples: { directors: 1, year: 1, runtime: 1 } for equality on directors, sort on year, range on runtime.
why_it_matters: The most prescriptive vendor rule for composite order.
notes: 9.0 docs. The $in threshold of 201 elements may change between versions.

title: MongoDB Database Manual: Shard Keys
engineering_principles: RECOMMENDED: choose a key that distributes documents evenly and facilitates common query patterns.
practical_examples: sh.shardCollection('sales.orders', { customerId: 'hashed' }).
why_it_matters: Poor keys cause jumbo chunks and uneven load.
notes: 9.0 docs.

title: MongoDB Database Manual: Choose a Shard Key
engineering_principles: RECOMMENDED: high cardinality, low value frequency, hashed sharding for monotonic keys, and keys present in common queries.
practical_examples: reshardCollection from 5.0; analyzeShardKey from 7.0.
why_it_matters: Supplies the core criteria for shard key rules.
notes: 9.0 docs. Scatter-gather can help large aggregations.

title: MongoDB Database Manual: Causal Consistency and Read and Write Concerns
engineering_principles: MANDATORY for all four guarantees with durability: majority read concern and majority write concern in causally consistent sessions.
practical_examples: Scenarios contrasting local with w:1 and majority combinations during a partition.
why_it_matters: Shows what session guarantees require once reads leave the primary.
notes: 9.0 docs. Does not discuss replication lag by name.

title: Use The Index, Luke: The Leaf Nodes
engineering_principles: Explanatory: leaf order is kept by links, so inserts avoid moving large amounts of data.
practical_examples: New node placed anywhere physically while pointers maintain order.
why_it_matters: Foundation for reasoning about range scans.
authority_rationale: Web edition of the recognized book SQL Performance Explained.
notes: Copyright 2010-2026.

title: Use The Index, Luke: Concatenated Indexes
engineering_principles: RECOMMENDED: choose column order so the index can be used as often as possible.
practical_examples: Index on employee and subsidiary IDs does not support searching on the second column alone.
why_it_matters: Usage-driven alternative to selectivity-first ordering.
authority_rationale: Web edition of the recognized book SQL Performance Explained.
notes: Copyright 2010-2026.

title: Use The Index, Luke: Myth Directory - Most Selective First
engineering_principles: RECOMMENDED: reject always-most-selective-first; selectivity should influence design only for independent range conditions.
practical_examples: Cites Guy Harrison, Jonathan Lewis and Gail Shaw against the rule.
why_it_matters: Primary citation for retiring this rule.
authority_rationale: Web edition of the recognized book SQL Performance Explained.
notes: Copyright 2010-2026.

title: Use The Index, Luke: Fetching the Next Page
engineering_principles: RECOMMENDED: seek pagination for deep or infinite scrolling, with a deterministic sort; it cannot fetch arbitrary pages.
practical_examples: Compare (sale_date, sale_id) with the last row seen.
why_it_matters: Pagination shape drives index key design.
authority_rationale: Web edition of the recognized book SQL Performance Explained.
notes: Row-value support statement references SQL Server 2017 and may be dated.

title: Use The Index, Luke: Case-Insensitive Search
engineering_principles: RECOMMENDED: index the exact expression used in the predicate.
practical_examples: CREATE INDEX emp_up_name ON employees (UPPER(last_name)).
why_it_matters: Explains non-SARGable predicates at schema level.
authority_rationale: Web edition of the recognized book SQL Performance Explained.
notes: Page has no implicit-conversion warning.

title: Use The Index, Luke: Nested Loops and the N+1 Problem
engineering_principles: RECOMMENDED: execute joins in the database; choose eager fetching per use case rather than as static configuration.
practical_examples: Hibernate fetch and Doctrine leftJoin.
why_it_matters: Round trips can outweigh data volume in response time.
authority_rationale: Web edition of the recognized book SQL Performance Explained.

title: "One Size Fits All": An Idea Whose Time Has Come and Gone
engineering_principles: Position paper: warehouse and OLTP workloads need different indexes, schemas and encoding; the market will fracture into independent engines.
practical_examples: StreamBase 160,000 messages per second versus 900 on a commercial RDBMS.
why_it_matters: Foundational basis for separate rule sets by workload.
notes: Text extracted from the fetched PDF. ICDE 2005 venue comes from the research brief, not the extracted text. Benchmark is authors' own.

title: C-Store: A Column-oriented DBMS
organization_author: Stonebraker, Abadi, Batkin, Chen, Cherniack, Ferreira, Lau, Lin, Madden, O'Neil, O'Neil, Rasin, Tran, Zdonik
engineering_principles: Design rationale: row stores are write-optimized and suit OLTP; column stores read only needed columns and suit ad-hoc warehouse queries.
practical_examples: Simplified TPC-H: 164x faster than a row store and 21x faster than a column store when space-constrained.
why_it_matters: Establishes the mechanics behind columnar warehouse schemas.
notes: Stanford mirror failed; VLDB archive copy used. Results are read-only, single-site, on 2005 hardware.

title: Designing Data-Intensive Applications (book site)
engineering_principles: Compares the fundamental ideas behind a broad variety of systems and their trade-offs.
practical_examples: None available from the fetched page.
why_it_matters: Standard reference for storage, replication and partitioning, though chapter text could not be verified here.
notes: Site copyright 2014-2019. O'Reilly chapter pages returned 403, so chapter-level claims in the notes are unverified.

title: Designing Data-Intensive Applications, 2nd Edition (announcement)
engineering_principles: Builds on the first edition, integrating new technologies and emerging trends.
practical_examples: None available from the fetched page.
why_it_matters: Identifies the current edition that framework citations should use.
authority_rationale: Recognized book, announced by its author.
notes: Publisher date March 2026 per page; O'Reilly's catalog listed February 2026 in search results. Chapter changes not described.

title: RocksDB Overview
engineering_principles: CONTEXTUAL: level compaction favors space amplification; universal favors write amplification at higher space and read amplification.
practical_examples: Prefix Bloom filters skip files lacking a prefix.
why_it_matters: Primary source for LSM tuning trade-offs.
authority_rationale: Official project documentation from a major engineering organization.
notes: Date is last wiki edit. No direct B-tree comparison on the page.

title: Citus Documentation: Choosing Distribution Column
engineering_principles: RECOMMENDED: tenant_id for multi-tenant apps, high-cardinality evenly distributed entity IDs for real-time apps; do not choose a timestamp as the distribution column.
practical_examples: Distribute by tenant or entity ID and use PostgreSQL partitioning for time.
why_it_matters: Separates shard key choice from time partitioning.
notes: Citus 13.0.1 docs.

title: Citus Documentation: Multi-tenant Applications
engineering_principles: MANDATORY in Citus: primary and foreign key constraints include the distribution column.
practical_examples: Composite keys including company_id; isolate_tenant_to_new_shard for large tenants.
why_it_matters: Sharding reshapes logical keys throughout the schema.
notes: Citus 13.0.1 docs.

title: Vitess Documentation: Sharding
engineering_principles: Sharding scheme is set by the Primary Vindex; resharding copies and verifies data while old shards serve traffic.
practical_examples: Shard names such as 80-c0; switchover with a few seconds of read-only downtime.
why_it_matters: Documents SQL scale-out and online rebalancing.
authority_rationale: Official documentation of a widely deployed scale-out system.
notes: Archived v22.0 docs; newer versions exist. No shard-size or 2PC content.

title: Vitess Documentation: Vindexes
engineering_principles: MANDATORY: a Primary Vindex must be unique. RECOMMENDED: functional unique vindexes as primary; secondary vindexes to avoid scatter.
practical_examples: Lookup Vindexes are too slow for resharding as Primary Vindexes.
why_it_matters: Pattern for alternate access paths in a sharded schema.
authority_rationale: Official documentation of a widely deployed scale-out system.
notes: Archived v22.0 docs.

title: Spanner: Schema design best practices
engineering_principles: RECOMMENDED: do not use a monotonic column as the first key part on high write rate tables; apply the same care to secondary indexes.
practical_examples: Hash modulo N ShardId column, swapped key order, bit-reversed sequences.
why_it_matters: Directly conflicts with single-node ever-increasing key advice.
notes: cloud.google.com URL redirects here.

title: CockroachDB: Understand Hotspots
engineering_principles: RECOMMENDED: random UUID keys or hash-sharded indexes for write spread, accepting costlier range reads that scan every shard.
practical_examples: SERIAL, TIMESTAMP and AUTO_INCREMENT columns concentrate writes at the index tail.
why_it_matters: Hotspots cannot be fixed by adding nodes, so key design matters.
notes: cockroachlabs.com URL redirects here.

title: TiDB: Explore HTAP
engineering_principles: CONTEXTUAL: add columnar replicas to selected tables for analytics on large data where row-store indexes are unusable or low selectivity.
practical_examples: Replicas must be specified per table; ETL simplification scenario below 100 TB and concurrency below 10.
why_it_matters: Represents the row-plus-columnar-replica HTAP design.
notes: v8.5 docs. Workload isolation is stated as a goal; no independent benchmark reviewed.

title: BigQuery: Introduction to partitioned tables
engineering_principles: RECOMMENDED: partition to reduce bytes read and estimate cost up front; cluster for finer granularity, multiple columns or high cardinality.
practical_examples: Partition expiration deletes whole partitions after a set period.
why_it_matters: Warehouse analogue of index and retention design.
notes: Partition limits are on a separate quotas page.

title: Snowflake: Clustering Keys and Clustered Tables
engineering_principles: CONTEXTUAL: define keys on typically multi-terabyte tables; use 3-4 columns or expressions, ordered lowest to highest cardinality.
practical_examples: Cast a timestamp to a date to reduce cardinality.
why_it_matters: Its cardinality ordering differs from B-tree reasoning.
notes: Most cost-effective for tables queried frequently that do not change frequently.

title: PgBouncer: Features
engineering_principles: CONTEXTUAL: transaction pooling only if the application avoids session-based features.
practical_examples: SET, LISTEN and session advisory locks unsupported in transaction mode; protocol-level prepared plans need max_prepared_statements above 0.
why_it_matters: Pooling mode constrains application session behaviour.
notes: Newest release listed is 1.26.1. Page does not call transaction pooling the suggested option.

title: HypoPG: Usage
engineering_principles: OPTIONAL: check whether the planner would use a candidate index before building it.
practical_examples: hypopg_create_index with a CREATE INDEX statement, then plain EXPLAIN.
why_it_matters: Low-cost index candidate testing on PostgreSQL.
notes: Example shows version 1.1.0. Supports btree, brin, hash and bloom.

title: PostgreSQL Wiki: Don't Do This
engineering_principles: RECOMMENDED: use NOT EXISTS over NOT IN subqueries, half-open timestamp ranges, and native partitioning over inheritance.
practical_examples: char(n) can unexpectedly prevent index use when a driver sends text parameters.
why_it_matters: Community list of type and query choices that hurt plans.
authority_rationale: Community-maintained reference from the project wiki.
notes: Date is last modified. No entries on FK indexing or UUIDs.

title: PostgreSQL Wiki: OptimizerHintsDiscussion
engineering_principles: RECOMMENDED by the community: avoid hints, which age badly across upgrades and data growth.
practical_examples: None beyond the listed objections.
why_it_matters: Reasoning for treating hints as a last resort.
authority_rationale: Community-maintained reference from the project wiki.
notes: Date is last modified; the position may be dated.

title: CQRS Pattern - Azure Architecture Center
engineering_principles: CONTEXTUAL: use where read and write needs diverge; not for simple domains or CRUD.
practical_examples: Write model publishes events through a transactional outbox to refresh a denormalized read store.
why_it_matters: Places denormalization in read models rather than the system of record.
authority_rationale: Architecture guidance from a major vendor.

title: Cache-Aside Pattern - Azure Architecture Center
engineering_principles: CONTEXTUAL: suits read-heavy data that tolerates staleness; update the store before removing the cached item.
practical_examples: Redis cache lookup with a five-minute expiry and key deletion after update.
why_it_matters: Defines consistency limits of a common read-scaling layer.
authority_rationale: Architecture guidance from a major vendor.

title: Azure Well-Architected Framework: Architecture strategies for optimizing scaling and partitioning
engineering_principles: RECOMMENDED: plan partitioning early, since retrofitting onto a live workload is harder; test scaling under production-like load.
practical_examples: Partition beyond a resource's upper scale limit; horizontal, vertical and functional options.
why_it_matters: General decision frame for scale-up versus scale-out.
authority_rationale: Architecture guidance from a major vendor.
